title: Anchor Argumentation Framework (prototype)
executive_summary: Compact prototype for a three-tier seller argumentation framework: Anchor -> Evidence -> Execution. Goal: give SEs and sellers a fast, repeatable way to lead discovery, land the technical claim, and close a micro-pilot ask in 15 minutes. Drafted for use in live demos, call scripts, and one-page battlecards.
background_and_problem: We have many partial battlecards and pilot scripts (see repo of drafts). Sellers ask: what is the single best way to transition from technical concern to pilot ask? Current materials are long and inconsistent. This doc experiments with a minimal, repeatable argument that supports: 1) rapid discovery, 2) provable economic claim, 3) low-friction pilot. Not a replacement for full playbooks—this is an in-call skeletal script that teams can layer onto existing decks.
framework_overview: Three tiers: 1) Anchor (value thread + 1-line claim), 2) Evidence (concise metrics / demo proof points), 3) Execution (micro-pilot ask + success criteria). Each tier contains a 15–30s script and a default fallback if the prospect pushes back. Designed for sellers who have 7–12 minutes technical time with an engineer or platform buyer.
anchor_prompts: Opening (15s): 'Most teams pick a single ML spend lever — latency, cost, or privacy. Which one matters most to you right now?'
One-liner claim (10s): 'Redwood's reserved routing + KV caching reduces per-inference cost up to 3x for short-form generation while keeping 95th% latency under 150ms.'
Why it matters (15s): 'That improvement either reduces run-rate or unlocks more queries, which directly affects ARR for search/chat use-cases.'
evidence_choices: Metric card: 'Observed pilot: 60% token cost reduction with prefix caching on a long-chat workload (sample customer X). Baseline: hosted API w/o KV cache.'
Latency card: 'Tail-latency guarantee: 95th% < 150ms on dedicated config — real logs from benchmark infra run 2025-08.'
Fallback evidence: 'If they challenge numbers, offer a scoped micro-benchmark during pilot week and share our perf dashboard template.'
execution_asks: Micro-pilot ask (30s): 'Let's run a 2-week micro-pilot: we ingest 2 canonical endpoints, run with preserved prompts, measure per-token cost & 95/99 latency. We'll provide a templated dashboard and a single rollback knob. Are you OK with a 2-week, low-commit spike test?'
Minimal success criteria: '1) cost improvement >= 25% OR 2) 95th% latency improvement >= 30% OR 3) stability parity with current infra.'
Data needs (quick): 'Access to sample traffic (2 endpoints), one engineer contact, and an API key/ingress for staging.'
common_objections_and_snippets: Objection: 'We can't share traffic.' — Snippet: 'We can run a synthetic micro-benchmark using anonymized prompt patterns, or execute a staging run with redacted data — both options are common and supported.'

Objection: 'Your numbers seem optimistic.' — Snippet: 'Totally fair. We commit to a live, repeatable micro-benchmark with your typical prompt mix. If you want, we do it alongside you in a shared runbook.'
Objection: 'We have regulatory constraints.' — Snippet: 'For regulated workloads we offer Private/VPC deployments with KMS integration and audit logs—pilot can run in your VPC with our runbook.'
play_examples: Use case A — Embedded search: Anchor on cost-per-query, evidence = token cost reduction from prefix cache + routing to quantized model, execution = 2-week query-sample pilot with SLO gating.
Use case B — Conversational assistant: Anchor on tail latency, evidence = dedicated throughput logs + 95/99 charts, execution = staged A/B rollout with fallback to hosted during peak hours.
Use case C — Regulated enterprise: Anchor on data isolation, evidence = private deployment checklist + audit log sample, execution = short on-prem proof with KMS stub and audit review.
metrics_and_signals_to_track: Primary: per-token cost delta (baseline vs pilot), measured daily
Primary: 95th and 99th percentile latency, measured across peak windows
Secondary: error rate / timeout incidents during pilot
Secondary: developer time to integrate (hours) and rollback events
seller_quick_card: One-liner claim + 3 evidence bullets + direct ask. Keep on top of call notes. Example text: 'We can show you a repeatable 25% unit cost win in 10 business days. If you like the result we'll scope reserved capacity & SLA.'
open_questions_and_risks: Unresolved: exact SLAs for small pilots; who signs off on test data access; playbook localization for EMEA procurement. Risk: sellers may overpromise the 3x number on short calls — add training slide for 'how to qualify the workload' in SE bootcamp.
